idea.why: A real crew, not a label: two specialist readers and one editor whose only job is folding both reports into a single ranked payload. Prompt injection is explicitly neutralised and empty-day behaviour is specified, which is what separates a designed shape from the first one that compiles.

structure.why: Every node type is the purpose-built one, no Code node anywhere, and the three parsers are not ceremony since each agent has a genuinely different contract. The only soft spot is that the merge carries no data the editor actually consumes.

connections.why: An exact map of the real dependencies, with equally clean sub-node wiring. executeOnce on the agents correctly neutralises the two items the append merge emits, so the barrier costs nothing.

answer.why: End to end it does what was asked, producing a page that is genuinely dashboard-shaped with email-safe table layout, inline styles, empty-state fallbacks and escaping on every interpolated value, then actually delivered. The one fair miss is a persistent view: it exists only as the morning email.

appraisal: What a multi-agent briefing should look like in n8n: the fan-out keeps the two fetches independent, each feeds a specialist with its own schema, and the streams rejoin at a merge before a single editor produces one ranked payload for rendering. The HTML is a real dashboard rather than a formatted list, with stat tiles, empty states and escaping on every field. The weakest seam is the merge: it correctly serves as a barrier, but the editor then ignores its items and re-reads both reports by node reference, so its data path is dead weight and the intent reads less clearly than it should. A knowledgeable user would have the editor consume the merged items directly, then add a webhook branch so the same HTML can be opened on demand.
